status.label: Reproduce stale MWB file clipboard
status.detail: Keyboard copying a second file can paste the first; timing/debounce is plausible but not demonstrated.

next_action.label: Compare rapid and delayed file-copy events
next_action.reason: Separate clipboard notification loss from file-path deduplication or transfer caching.

judgment.rationale: The public sequence copies file A successfully, keyboard-copies file B and receives A again; context-menu copying reportedly recovers. No timing is specified, so a one-second guard is not yet a proven cause.
evidence: The PowerToys 0.80 report supplies file A/B and keyboard-versus-context-menu behavior; there are no public comments.
FormHelper.cs handles clipboard notifications with a one-second recent-event guard.
Clipboard.cs CheckClipboardEx contains another one-second check and file-path/string deduplication and LastDragDropFile state.
The broad MWB tracker is not a targeted fix or active implementation for this scenario.
judgment.recommended_action: Reproduce with distinct harmless files using controlled intervals and trace notification, clipboard sequence and transfer identity.

fix_assessment.rationale: The clipboard pipeline has concrete timing/cache boundaries to inspect; no linked fix covers the supplied A/B sequence.

proposed_fixes.title: Ensure the latest MWB file clipboard reaches the peer
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Hypothesis: a clipboard change is discarded by timing guards or stale path/transfer deduplication. The report does not state its copy interval, so attributing the issue specifically to the one-second guard would be premature.
plan: Reproduce file A followed by distinct file B at intervals below one second and above two seconds, comparing keyboard and context-menu copy.
Trace native clipboard sequence/change identity, both guard decisions, CheckClipboardEx deduplication and the advertised/transferred file identity.

If a latest change is lost, replace the confirmed drop-only boundary with processing of the latest pending clipboard state; if caching is responsible, invalidate the confirmed stale transfer/path state.
Preserve clipboard-loop suppression and avoid clearing legitimate clipboard ownership or repeating large transfers.
Add regressions for rapid A/B/C changes, delayed changes, repeated same-file copy and peer reconnect.
verification: After copying B, the peer pastes B's distinct name and content rather than A.
Rapid updates converge on the latest file without loops or duplicate transfers.
Text/image clipboard and ordinary same-file behavior do not regress.

confidence.rationale: The supplied sequence and inspected event/cache guards support a narrow investigation, but no trace connects the reported keyboard-only behavior to a particular guard.

issue_context.summary: Mouse Without Borders can paste the previously copied file after keyboard-copying a new file; context-menu recopying reportedly refreshes it.
known_information: The report identifies PowerToys 0.80 and a two-file copy/paste sequence.
No interval between copies or diagnostic conclusion is supplied.
The owning source has both timing suppression and file-path/transfer-state deduplication.
inferences: A lost change and stale transfer identity can produce the same symptom and require separate traces.
issue_context.analysis: The reporter's sequence is sufficient for a maintainer two-PC experiment with generated safe files. Generic logs or personal sample files are not required.
initial_investigation: Read the full issue and empty discussion and checked obvious linked work.
Inspected CheckClipboardEx and file clipboard state in Clipboard.cs.

actions.label: Review latest-file clipboard plan
actions.description: Approve the bounded notification/cache investigation before changing debounce behavior.

prerequisites: Use two physical PCs with matching current versions and working file clipboard sharing.
Prepare a development build with clipboard-change/transfer-identity instrumentation and harmless small files with distinct names and content.
steps: Keyboard-copy A on the source and paste on the peer; verify name and content.
Keyboard-copy B more than two seconds later and paste on the peer.
Repeat A then B less than one second apart and compare with context-menu copy.
Repeat rapid A/B/C updates while tracing whether B/C is observed, suppressed, advertised and transferred.
reproduce.expected_result: The peer pastes the latest successfully copied file, independent of keyboard/context-menu activation.
reproduce.setup_prompt: Create three small test text files named MWB-A, MWB-B and MWB-C with visibly distinct non-sensitive contents. Prepare timestamped copy actions at controlled intervals on two physical PCs; do not use personal files.
